From babab1b42ed68877ef669a08384becf281ad2582 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jie Zhang <jzhang918@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 17:50:32 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] net: stmmac: fix oops when split header is enabled

For GMAC4, when split header is enabled, in some rare cases, the
hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload.
Thus we cannot assume buf2 is always fully filled if it is not
the last descriptor. Otherwise, the length of buf2 of the second
descriptor will be calculated wrong and cause an oops:

Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffff00019246bfc0
...
x2 : 0000000000000040 x1 : ffff00019246bfc0 x0 : ffff00009246c000
Call trace:
 dcache_inval_poc+0x28/0x58 (P)
 dma_direct_sync_single_for_cpu+0x38/0x6c
 __dma_sync_single_for_cpu+0x34/0x6c
 stmmac_napi_poll_rx+0x8f0/0xb60
 __napi_poll.constprop.0+0x30/0x144
 net_rx_action+0x160/0x274
 handle_softirqs+0x1b8/0x1fc
...

To fix this, the PL bit-field in RDES3 register is used for all
descriptors, whether it is the last descriptor or not.

Fixes: ec222003bd94 ("net: stmmac: Prepare to add Split Header support")
Reviewed-by: Jacob Keller <jacob.e.keller@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jie Zhang <jie.zhang@analog.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260209225037.589130-1-jie.zhang@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/stmmac_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/stmmac_main.c
index c63099a77cc0..82375d34ad57 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/stmmac_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/stmmac_main.c
@@ -5040,13 +5040,27 @@ static unsigned int stmmac_rx_buf2_len(struct stmmac_priv *priv,
 	if (!priv->sph_active)
 		return 0;
 
-	/* Not last descriptor */
-	if (status & rx_not_ls)
+	/* For GMAC4, when split header is enabled, in some rare cases, the
+	 * hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload.
+	 * Thus we cannot assume buf2 is always fully filled if it is not
+	 * the last descriptor. Otherwise, the length of buf2 of the second
+	 * descriptor will be calculated wrong and cause an oops.
+	 *
+	 * If this is the last descriptor, 'plen' is the length of the
+	 * received packet that was transferred to system memory.
+	 * Otherwise, it is the accumulated number of bytes that have been
+	 * transferred for the current packet.
+	 *
+	 * Thus 'plen - len' always gives the correct length of buf2.
+	 */
+
+	/* Not GMAC4 and not last descriptor */
+	if (priv->plat->core_type != DWMAC_CORE_GMAC4 && (status & rx_not_ls))
 		return priv->dma_conf.dma_buf_sz;
 
+	/* GMAC4 or last descriptor */
 	plen = stmmac_get_rx_frame_len(priv, p, coe);
 
-	/* Last descriptor */
 	return plen - len;
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of Modifications:**

**File modified:** `drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/stmmac_main.c`

- **Change in function `stmmac_rx_buf2_len()`**  
  Updated the logic for calculating the length of `buf2` (the payload buffer) when split header is enabled.  
  - **Before:** For all non-last descriptors, the function returned the full DMA buffer size (`dma_buf_sz`), assuming `buf2` was always fully filled.  
  - **After:**  
    - For cores other than GMAC4 (i.e., `DWMAC_CORE_GMAC4`) and when the descriptor is **not** the last, the original behavior (return `dma_buf_sz`) is retained.  
    - For GMAC4 (regardless of being last or not) **and** for last descriptors of any core, the length is computed as `plen - len`, where `plen` is the total payload length reported by hardware and `len` is the header length.  
  - **Reason:** On GMAC4, in rare cases the hardware may not fill `buf2` of the first descriptor even if it is not the last. Using `plen` (which accumulates bytes transferred) correctly reflects the actual data in `buf2` and prevents incorrect length calculations that lead to a kernel oops (e.g., invalid page requests during DMA sync).

- **Comments updated**  
  Added explanatory comments describing the hardware anomaly and why the new calculation is correct for GMAC4.

**Relationships among modifications:**  
The entire fix is self-contained within a single function (`stmmac_rx_buf2_len`) of a single file. The change directly addresses a specific hardware errata for the GMAC4 core when split header is active. No other files or functions are affected.

net: stmmac: fix oops when split header is enabled

For GMAC4, when split header is enabled, in some rare cases, the
hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload.
Thus we cannot assume buf2 is always fully filled if it is not

Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffff00019246bfc0
...

Call trace:
 dcache_inval_poc+0x28/0x58 (P)
 dma_direct_sync_single_for_cpu+0x38/0x6c
 __dma_sync_single_for_cpu+0x34/0x6c

To fix this, the PL bit-field in RDES3 register is used for all
descriptors, whether it is the last descriptor or not.

Fixes: ec222003bd94 ("net: stmmac: Prepare to add Split Header support")
Reviewed-by: Jacob Keller <jacob.e.keller@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jie Zhang <jie.zhang@analog.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260209225037.589130-1-jie.zhang@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
On GMAC4 with split header enabled, the hardware may not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload in some rare cases. The original code incorrectly assumed that for non-last descriptors, buf2 is always fully filled (returning dma_buf_sz). This assumption leads to wrong length calculation for buf2 of the second descriptor, causing a kernel oops due to invalid memory access during DMA synchronization.

Here is the patch:
 
 static unsigned int stmmac_rx_buf2_len(struct stmmac_priv *priv,
 				       struct dma_desc *p,
 				       int status, unsigned int len)
 {
 	int coe = priv->hw->rx_csum;
 	unsigned int plen = 0;
 
 	/* Not split header, buffer is not available */
 	if (!priv->sph_active)
 		return 0;
 
-	/* Not last descriptor */
-	if (status & rx_not_ls)
+	/* For GMAC4, when split header is enabled, in some rare cases, the
+	 * hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload.
+	 * Thus we cannot assume buf2 is always fully filled if it is not
+	 * the last descriptor. Otherwise, the length of buf2 of the second
+	 * descriptor will be calculated wrong and cause an oops.
+	 *
+	 * If this is the last descriptor, 'plen' is the length of the
+	 * received packet that was transferred to system memory.
+	 * Otherwise, it is the accumulated number of bytes that have been
+	 * transferred for the current packet.
+	 *
+	 * Thus 'plen - len' always gives the correct length of buf2.
+	 */
+
+	/* Not GMAC4 and not last descriptor */
+	if (priv->plat->core_type != DWMAC_CORE_GMAC4 && (status & rx_not_ls))
 		return priv->dma_conf.dma_buf_sz;
 
+	/* GMAC4 or last descriptor */
 	plen = stmmac_get_rx_frame_len(priv, p, coe);
 
-	/* Last descriptor */
 	return plen - len;
 }
